```{r}
# Input parameters - fixed

n<- 24 # population size
ct.rates<-2 # avg number of daily contacts per day
nSeeds<-1 # number of cases starting the epidemic
R0<-1.5 # average number of secondary cases generated per infected individual in a fully susceptible population
inf.param<- R0/(ct.rates)
# pathogen<-"COVID-19" # or "FLU"
t.stop  <- 360 # maximum number of days the simulation is running (if infected cases present)


# Compute the reproduction number related to the selected network. 
source("F:\\Statistics UHasselt\\Semester 4\\Master Thesis\\Master-Thesis---Chau-\\EKPmodify_group.R")
nSim<-100
nSeed<-22032026
set.seed(nSeed)

baseline_results <- list() 
group_results <- list() 
strict_results <- list()

for (i in 1:nSim) {
  print(i)
  
  # SCENARIO 1: Free mixing (baseline)
  baseline_results[[i]] <- sim.epi(
    n = n, ct.rates = ct.rates, nSeeds = 1, inf.param = inf.param, t.stop = t.stop)
  
  # SCENARIO 2: Staff-Bridge - Volunteers in rooms + Staff moving between
  # IDs 1-10: Volunteers Group A | IDs 11-20: Volunteers Group B | IDs 21-24: Staff
  volunteers_a <- 10
  volunteers_b <- 10
  staff  <- 4
  
  scenario2 <- c(rep(1, volunteers_a), rep(2, volunteers_b), rep(3, staff))
  
  # Mixing Matrix (M) for 3 groups:
  # Rows = Infector Group, Cols = Potential Infectee Group
  # Probabilities should represent the likelihood of contact
  M_matrix <- matrix(c(
    0.90, 0.00, 0.10,  # Group 1 (Volunteers A) stays in Room A (90%), only sees Staff (10%)
    0.00, 0.90, 0.10,  # Group 2 (Volunteers B) stays in Room B (90%), only sees Staff (10%)
    0.40, 0.40, 0.20   # Group 3 (Staff) visits A (40%), B (40%), and other Staff (20%)
  ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  
  seed_id <- sample(1:10, 1)

  group_results[[i]] <- sim.epi(
    n = n, ct.rates = ct.rates, 
    nSeeds = 1, # Assume Infector is located in Volunteers A (ID 1-10)
    inf.param = inf.param, t.stop = t.stop, 
    group_assign = scenario2, M = M_matrix)

  # SCENARIO 3: Strict Cohorting - Staff A for Group A, Staff B for Group B
  # n=24: 10 Volunteers A, 10 Volunteers B, 2 Staff A, 2 Staff B
  volunteers_room <- 10
  staff_room <- 2
  
  # Group 1: Volunteers A | Group 2: Volunteers B | Group 3: Staff A | Group 4: Staff B
  scenario3 <- c(rep(1, volunteers_room), rep(2, volunteers_room), 
                     rep(3, staff_room), rep(4, staff_room))
  
  # Matrix M for 4 groups: Staff A (Group 3) only meets Volunteers A (Group 1). Staff B (Group 4) only meets Volunteers B (Group 2).
  # There is no overlap between Group (1,3) and Group (2,4).
  M_strict <- matrix(c(
    0.90, 0.00, 0.10, 0.00,  # Group 1 (Volunteers A) stays in Room A (90%), only sees Staff A (10%)
    0.00, 0.90, 0.00, 0.10,  # Group 2 (Volunteers B) stays in Room B (90%), only sees Staff B (10%)
    0.50, 0.00, 0.50, 0.00,  # Group 3 (Staff A) visits A (50%), and other Staff A (50%)
    0.00, 0.50, 0.00, 0.50   # Group 3 (Staff B) visits B (50%), and other Staff B (50%)
  ), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)

  strict_results[[i]] <- sim.epi(
    n = n, ct.rates = ct.rates, 
    nSeeds = 1, # Assume Infector is located in Volunteers A (ID 1-10)
    inf.param = inf.param, t.stop = t.stop, 
    group_assign = scenario3, M = M_strict)
}


```



```{r}

analyze_results_sir <- function(results_list, n, t.stop) {
  
  # 1. Total Attack Rate
  # Count everyone who is NOT Susceptible (0), 
  # meaning they are either Infected (1) or Recovered (-1)
  attack_rates <- sapply(results_list, function(res) {
    if (is.null(res$status.matrix)) return(0)
    sum(res$status.matrix$infected != 0) / n
  })
  
  # 2. Daily Infection Incidence
  # In your SIR code, Event '1' represents the moment of infection
  inc_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(results_list), ncol = t.stop + 1)
  
  for (i in 1:length(results_list)) {
    time_events <- results_list[[i]]$time.events
    
    # Check if any infection events occurred
    if (!is.null(time_events) && nrow(time_events) > 0) {
      # Filter for event type 1 (Infection)
      inf_times <- time_events[time_events[, 2] == 1, 1]
      
      if (length(inf_times) > 0) {
        # Group by floor of time to get daily counts
        tab <- table(factor(floor(inf_times), levels = 0:t.stop))
        inc_matrix[i, ] <- as.numeric(tab)
      }
    }
  }
  
  avg_daily_inc <- colMeans(inc_matrix)
  
  # 3. Outbreak Probability
  # Probability that more than 10% of the population gets infected
  outbreak_prob <- mean(attack_rates > 0.10)
  
  return(list(
    attack_raw = attack_rates,
    mean_attack = mean(attack_rates),
    daily_inc = avg_daily_inc,
    outbreak_prob = outbreak_prob
  ))
}

# Run the analysis for each scenario
# Make sure your simulation lists (baseline_results, etc.) are already populated
summary_baseline <- analyze_results_sir(baseline_results, n, t.stop)
summary_group    <- analyze_results_sir(group_results, n, t.stop)
summary_strict  <- analyze_results_sir(strict_results, n, t.stop)

# Create the summary comparison table
comparison_table <- data.frame(
  Scenario = c("Free Mixing", "Staff-Bridge", "Strict-Cohorting"),
  Avg_Attack_Rate = c(
    summary_baseline$mean_attack, 
    summary_group$mean_attack, 
    summary_strict$mean_attack
  ),
  Outbreak_Probability = c(
    summary_baseline$outbreak_prob, 
    summary_group$outbreak_prob, 
    summary_strict$outbreak_prob
  )
)

print(comparison_table)

```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Updated function for SIR logic
get_cum_30_days_sir <- function(results_list, n, scenario_name) {
  t_limit <- 30
  # Initialize matrix to store cumulative counts for each simulation
  cum_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(results_list), ncol = t_limit + 1)
  
  for (i in 1:length(results_list)) {
    time_events <- results_list[[i]]$time.events
    
    if (!is.null(time_events) && nrow(time_events) > 0) {
      # Filter rows where event code is 1
      inf_times <- time_events[time_events[, 2] == 1, 1]
      
      if (length(inf_times) > 0) {
        # Tabulate infections occurring each day from 0 to 30
        daily_counts <- table(factor(floor(inf_times), levels = 0:t_limit))
        
        # Calculate cumulative proportion of the population infected
        # We add the initial seeds (nSeeds) if they aren't captured as events at t=0
        cum_matrix[i, ] <- cumsum(as.numeric(daily_counts)) / n
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Return summarized data frame with the mean across all simulations
  return(data.frame(
    Day = 0:t_limit,
    Cumulative_Rate = colMeans(cum_matrix),
    Scenario = scenario_name
  ))
}

# Extract and process data for the 3 scenarios
df1 <- get_cum_30_days_sir(baseline_results, n, "Free Mixing")
df2 <- get_cum_30_days_sir(group_results, n, "Staff-Bridge")
df3 <- get_cum_30_days_sir(strict_results, n, "Strict-Cohorting")

# Combine datasets
plot_data_30 <- rbind(df1, df2, df3)

# Create the Visualization
ggplot(plot_data_30, aes(x = Day, y = Cumulative_Rate, color = Scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + # 'size' is deprecated in newer ggplot2, use 'linewidth'
  geom_point(size = 2) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Early Phase: Cumulative Attack Rate (First 30 Days)",
    subtitle = "SIR Model Comparison: Impact of Population Structure",
    x = "Day",
    y = "Cumulative Proportion Infected (%)",
    color = "Model Scenarios"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom", 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
calculate_metrics_sir <- function(results_list, n) {
  
  # Cumulative cases (Anyone who was infected (1) or recovered (-1))
  cum_cases_vec <- sapply(results_list, function(res) {
    if (is.null(res$status.matrix)) return(0)
    sum(res$status.matrix$infected != 0)
  })
  
  # Daily generated cases (Average cases per unit of time)
  daily_gen_vec <- sapply(results_list, function(res) {
    # CHANGE: Count event type 1 (Infection) instead of 0.5
    inf_events <- sum(res$time.events[,2] == 1)
    
    # Calculate duration of the outbreak
    max_t <- if(nrow(res$time.events) > 0) max(res$time.events[,1]) else 0
    
    if (max_t > 0) {
      return(inf_events / max_t)
    } else {
      return(0)
    }
  })
  
  # Transmission ratio (Proportion of total cases that were NOT seeds)
  trans_ratio_vec <- sapply(results_list, function(res) {
    total_inf <- sum(res$status.matrix$infected != 0)
    # Seeds are those whose infection time is exactly 0
    seeds <- sum(res$status.matrix$time.of.infection == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    if (total_inf > seeds) {
      return((total_inf - seeds) / total_inf) 
    } else {
      return(0)
    }
  })
  
  # Return summarized results as a named character vector
  return(c(
    Avg_Daily_Cases = round(mean(daily_gen_vec), 2),
    Cumulative_Cases = round(mean(cum_cases_vec), 0),
    Cumulative_Perc = paste0(round((mean(cum_cases_vec)/n)*100, 1), "%"),
    Transmission_Ratio = round(mean(trans_ratio_vec), 2)
  ))
}

# Calculate for each Scenario
scn1_metrics <- calculate_metrics_sir(baseline_results, n)
scn2_metrics <- calculate_metrics_sir(group_results, n)
scn3_metrics <- calculate_metrics_sir(strict_results, n)

# Create the summary table structure
summary_table_final <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Average daily generated cases", 
             "Cumulative cases", 
             "Cumulative cases percentage", 
             "Transmission ratio"),
  Scn.1 = scn1_metrics,
  Scn.2 = scn2_metrics,
  Scn.3 = scn3_metrics,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Helper to calculate percentage change compared to Scn.1 (Baseline)
calc_change <- function(val_str, ref_str) {
  val <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", val_str)) # Remove % or other chars if any
  ref <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", ref_str))
  
  if (ref == 0) return(paste0(val_str, " (N/A)"))
  
  change <- ((val - ref) / ref) * 100
  sign <- if(change > 0) "+" else ""
  return(paste0(val_str, " (", sign, round(change, 0), "%)"))
}

# Apply change calculations for the first row (Daily Cases)
summary_table_final[1, "Scn.2"] <- calc_change(scn2_metrics[1], scn1_metrics[1])
summary_table_final[1, "Scn.3"] <- calc_change(scn3_metrics[1], scn1_metrics[1])

# Display the results
print(summary_table_final)
```

```{r}
# Find the index of the worst simulation
find_worst_sim <- function(results_list) {

# Count the number of infected people (status != 0) for each simulation
inf_counts <- sapply(results_list, function(res) {
sum(res$status.matrix$infected != 0)
})

# Find the location (index) with the highest number of infections
max_idx <- which.max(inf_counts)
max_val <- inf_counts[max_idx]
return(list(index = max_idx, count = max_val))
}

# 3 worst scenarios
worst_baseline <- find_worst_sim(baseline_results)
worst_group <- find_worst_sim(group_results)
worst_strict <- find_worst_sim(strict_results)

# Print results
cat("Free Mixing Scenario: Simulation number", worst_baseline$index, "has", worst_baseline$count, "cases.\n")
cat("Staff-Bridge Scenario: Simulation number", worst_group$index, "has", worst_group$count, "cases.\n")
cat("Strict-Cohorting Scenario: Simulation number", worst_strict$index, "has", worst_strict$count, "cases.\n")

# View of the Staff-Bridge scenario table in worst simulation
View(group_results[[worst_baseline$index]]$status.matrix)
View(group_results[[worst_group$index]]$status.matrix)
View(group_results[[worst_strict$index]]$status.matrix)
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot attack rate and extinction probability

# Compute attack rates
att.rate <- data.frame(attack_rate = numeric(nSim))

for(i in 1:nSim) {
  total_inf <- length(which(epi.outbreak[[i]]$status.matrix$infected==-1))
  att.rate$attack_rate[i] <- total_inf / n
}

# Metrics
extinction_threshold <- 0.10 #here we assume that and outbreak goes extinct if less
# than 10% of the population is ultimately infected
att.rate$is_extinct <- att.rate$attack_rate < extinction_threshold
extinction_rate <- mean(att.rate$is_extinct)
non_extinct_ar <- att.rate$attack_rate[!att.rate$is_extinct]

# Plotting
par(mfrow=c(1, 3))

# Panel A: All Attack Rates
hist(att.rate$attack_rate, main="Total Attack Rate", xlab="Proportion Infected", col="skyblue")

# Panel B: Extinction Rate
barplot(c(Extinct = extinction_rate, Major = 1 - extinction_rate), 
        main="Outbreak Outcome", col=c("grey", "orange"), ylab="Probability")

# Panel C: Attack Rate (Non-extinct outbreaks)
hist(non_extinct_ar, main="AR (Non-Extinct)", xlab="Proportion Infected", col="orange")
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot Transmission tree
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (dev.cur() != 1) dev.off()
library(igraph)
total_cases <- sapply(epi.outbreak, function(x) sum(x$status.matrix$infected != 0))
w <- which.max(total_cases)
plot_data <- epi.outbreak[[w]]
plot_transmission_network <- function(sim_output) {
  
  sm <- sim_output$status.matrix
  
  # --- 1. Data Prep ---
  infected_indices <- which(sm$infected != 0)
  if(length(infected_indices) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  nodes <- sm[infected_indices, ]
  nodes$infected_id <- as.character(nodes$infected_id)
  nodes$infector <- as.character(nodes$infector)
  
  nodes <- nodes[, c("infected_id", "time.of.infection", "infector")]
  edges <- nodes[!is.na(nodes$infector), c("infector", "infected_id")]
  g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, vertices = nodes, directed = TRUE)
  
  # --- 2. Initial Layout ---
  l <- layout_as_tree(g, flip.y = FALSE)
  l[,1] <- V(g)$time.of.infection
  
  # --- 3. First Pass: Rough Grouping & Spacing ---
  # Group nodes by integer time steps
  time_bin <- 1.0 
  l_df <- data.frame(id=1:nrow(l), x=l[,1], y=l[,2])
  l_df$group <- round(l_df$x / time_bin)
  
  unique_grps <- sort(unique(l_df$group))
  
  min_y_gap <- 5.0 
  
  for(g_id in unique_grps) {
    idx <- which(l_df$group == g_id)
    if(length(idx) > 0) {
      curr_y <- l_df$y[idx]
      ord <- order(curr_y)
      idx_sorted <- idx[ord]
      n <- length(idx)
      
      span <- (n - 1) * min_y_gap
      new_y <- seq(-span/2, span/2, length.out = n)
      l_df$y[idx_sorted] <- new_y
    }
  }
  l[,2] <- l_df$y
  
  # --- 4. Second Pass: Collision Repulsion ---
  n_nodes <- nrow(l)
  
  # If nodes are closer than X=1.5 and Y=2.5, push them apart.
  thresh_x <- 1.5 
  thresh_y <- 2.5
  
  # Iterate to resolve overlaps
  for(iter in 1:50) {
    moved <- FALSE
    for(i in 1:(n_nodes-1)) {
      for(j in (i+1):n_nodes) {
        
        dx <- abs(l[i,1] - l[j,1])
        dy <- abs(l[i,2] - l[j,2])
        
        # Check strict overlap
        if(dx < thresh_x && dy < thresh_y) {
          
          overlap <- thresh_y - dy
          shift <- overlap / 2 + 0.1 # Push them apart
          
          if(l[i,2] >= l[j,2]) {
            l[i,2] <- l[i,2] + shift
            l[j,2] <- l[j,2] - shift
          } else {
            l[i,2] <- l[i,2] - shift
            l[j,2] <- l[j,2] + shift
          }
          moved <- TRUE
        }
      }
    }
    if(!moved) break 
  }
  
  # --- 5. Plot Limits ---
  x_range <- range(l[,1])
  y_range <- range(l[,2])
  
  x_limits <- c(x_range[1] - 1, x_range[2] + 2)
  max_y <- max(abs(y_range)) + 1 # Add buffer
  y_limits <- c(-max_y, max_y)
  
  # --- 6. Plotting ---
  plot(g, 
       layout = l,
       rescale = FALSE, 
       asp = 0,         
       xlim = x_limits, 
       ylim = y_limits,   
       
       vertex.shape = "circle", 
       vertex.size = 50,         
       vertex.color = "white", 
       vertex.frame.color = NA, 
       
       vertex.label = V(g)$name,
       vertex.label.color = "black",
       vertex.label.font = 2,
       vertex.label.cex = 1,
       
       edge.color = "firebrick",
       edge.width = 1.0,
       edge.arrow.size = 0.35,
       edge.curved = 0.2,       
       
       main = "Transmission Tree"
  )
  
  axis(1, at = pretty(x_limits), col = "gray40", col.axis = "gray40")
  mtext("Time (Days)", side = 1, line = 2.5, col = "gray40")
  
}
plot_transmission_network(plot_data)
```

```{r}
#Input parameters - fixed

n<- 24 #population size
ct.rates<-5 #avg number of daily contacts per day
nSeeds<-1 #number of cases starting the epidemic
R0<-1.5 # average number of secondary cases generated per infected individual in a fully susceptible population
inf.param<- R0/(ct.rates)
#pathogen<-"COVID-19" # or "FLU"

#Compute the reproduction number related to the selected network. 
source("F:\\Statistics UHasselt\\Semester 4\\Master Thesis\\Master-Thesis---Chau-\\EKPmodify.R")
nSim<-100
epi.outbreak<-list()
nSeed<-1062021
set.seed(nSeed)

# Fixed contact network (random network Erdos-Renyi)
A <- make_network_er(n = 24, p = 0.15)

for (i in 1:nSim){
  print(i)
  
  epi.outbreak[[i]] <- sim.epi(
  n = n,
  ct.rates = 2,
  nSeeds = 1,
  inf.param = inf.param,
  t.stop = t.stop,
  k = 0.2,
  nu_mean = 4.5,
  nu_sd = 2.0,
  mean_ip = 6,
  sd_ip = 2,
  A = A
)
}

library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
  # Iterate to resolve overlaps
  for(iter in 1:50) {
    moved <- FALSE
    for(i in 1:(n_nodes-1)) {
      for(j in (i+1):n_nodes) {
        
        dx <- abs(l[i,1] - l[j,1])
        dy <- abs(l[i,2] - l[j,2])
        
        # Check strict overlap
        if(dx < thresh_x && dy < thresh_y) {
          
          overlap <- thresh_y - dy
          shift <- overlap / 2 + 0.1 # Push them apart
          
          if(l[i,2] >= l[j,2]) {
            l[i,2] <- l[i,2] + shift
            l[j,2] <- l[j,2] - shift
          } else {
            l[i,2] <- l[i,2] - shift
            l[j,2] <- l[j,2] + shift
          }
          moved <- TRUE
        }
      }
    }
    if(!moved) break 
  }
  
  # --- 5. Plot Limits ---
  x_range <- range(l[,1])
  y_range <- range(l[,2])
  
  x_limits <- c(x_range[1] - 1, x_range[2] + 2)
  max_y <- max(abs(y_range)) + 1 # Add buffer
  y_limits <- c(-max_y, max_y)
  
  # --- 6. Plotting ---
  plot(g, 
       layout = l,
       rescale = FALSE, 
       asp = 0,         
       xlim = x_limits, 
       ylim = y_limits,   
       
       vertex.shape = "circle", 
       vertex.size = 50,         
       vertex.color = "white", 
       vertex.frame.color = NA, 
       
       vertex.label = V(g)$name,
       vertex.label.color = "black",
       vertex.label.font = 2,
       vertex.label.cex = 1,
       
       edge.color = "firebrick",
       edge.width = 1.0,
       edge.arrow.size = 0.35,
       edge.curved = 0.2,       
       
       main = "Transmission Tree"
  )
  
  axis(1, at = pretty(x_limits), col = "gray40", col.axis = "gray40")
  mtext("Time (Days)", side = 1, line = 2.5, col = "gray40")
  
}
plot_transmission_network(plot_data)
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot Transmission tree
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (dev.cur() != 1) dev.off()
library(igraph)
total_cases <- sapply(epi.outbreak, function(x) sum(x$status.matrix$infected != 0))
w <- which.max(total_cases)
plot_data <- epi.outbreak[[w]]
plot_transmission_network <- function(sim_output) {
  
  sm <- sim_output$status.matrix
  
  # --- 1. Data Prep ---
  infected_indices <- which(sm$infected != 0)
  if(length(infected_indices) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  nodes <- sm[infected_indices, ]
  nodes$infected_id <- as.character(nodes$infected_id)
  nodes$infector <- as.character(nodes$infector)
  
  nodes <- nodes[, c("infected_id", "time.of.infection", "infector")]
  edges <- nodes[!is.na(nodes$infector), c("infector", "infected_id")]
  g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, vertices = nodes, directed = TRUE)
  
  # --- 2. Initial Layout ---
  l <- layout_as_tree(g, flip.y = FALSE)
  l[,1] <- V(g)$time.of.infection
  
  # --- 3. First Pass: Rough Grouping & Spacing ---
  # Group nodes by integer time steps
  time_bin <- 1.0 
  l_df <- data.frame(id=1:nrow(l), x=l[,1], y=l[,2])
  l_df$group <- round(l_df$x / time_bin)
  
  unique_grps <- sort(unique(l_df$group))
  
  min_y_gap <- 5.0 
  
  for(g_id in unique_grps) {
    idx <- which(l_df$group == g_id)
    if(length(idx) > 0) {
      curr_y <- l_df$y[idx]
      ord <- order(curr_y)
      idx_sorted <- idx[ord]
      n <- length(idx)
      
      span <- (n - 1) * min_y_gap
      new_y <- seq(-span/2, span/2, length.out = n)
      l_df$y[idx_sorted] <- new_y
    }
  }
  l[,2] <- l_df$y
  
  # --- 4. Second Pass: Collision Repulsion ---
  n_nodes <- nrow(l)
  
  # If nodes are closer than X=1.5 and Y=2.5, push them apart.
  thresh_x <- 1.5 
  thresh_y <- 2.5
  
  # Iterate to resolve overlaps
  for(iter in 1:50) {
    moved <- FALSE
    for(i in 1:(n_nodes-1)) {
      for(j in (i+1):n_nodes) {
        
        dx <- abs(l[i,1] - l[j,1])
        dy <- abs(l[i,2] - l[j,2])
        
        # Check strict overlap
        if(dx < thresh_x && dy < thresh_y) {
          
          overlap <- thresh_y - dy
          shift <- overlap / 2 + 0.1 # Push them apart
          
          if(l[i,2] >= l[j,2]) {
            l[i,2] <- l[i,2] + shift
            l[j,2] <- l[j,2] - shift
          } else {
            l[i,2] <- l[i,2] - shift
            l[j,2] <- l[j,2] + shift
          }
          moved <- TRUE
        }
      }
    }
    if(!moved) break 
  }
  
  # --- 5. Plot Limits ---
  x_range <- range(l[,1])
  y_range <- range(l[,2])
  
  x_limits <- c(x_range[1] - 1, x_range[2] + 2)
  max_y <- max(abs(y_range)) + 1 # Add buffer
  y_limits <- c(-max_y, max_y)
  
  # --- 6. Plotting ---
  plot(g, 
       layout = l,
       rescale = FALSE, 
       asp = 0,         
       xlim = x_limits, 
       ylim = y_limits,   
       
       vertex.shape = "circle", 
       vertex.size = 50,         
       vertex.color = "white", 
       vertex.frame.color = NA, 
       
       vertex.label = V(g)$name,
       vertex.label.color = "black",
       vertex.label.font = 2,
       vertex.label.cex = 1,
       
       edge.color = "firebrick",
       edge.width = 1.0,
       edge.arrow.size = 0.35,
       edge.curved = 0.2,       
       
       main = "Transmission Tree"
  )
  
  axis(1, at = pretty(x_limits), col = "gray40", col.axis = "gray40")
  mtext("Time (Days)", side = 1, line = 2.5, col = "gray40")
  
}
plot_transmission_network(plot_data)
```
